reader.requirement: At 1985 (level 2) RESERVE integer-1 [AREA | AREAS] on a file control entry makes the connector allocate exactly integer-1 input-output areas, and without the clause the implementor's count; integer-1 is an unsigned nonzero integer (the 1985 III.2 integer), so RESERVE 0 is refused, and the clause applies to every organization the 1985 modules give it. The witness covers RESERVE on every organization with the records passing through unchanged; the area count itself is not observable to the program.

reader.notes: The binder captures integer-1, the emitter registers it with the connector only when the clause is written, and each organization sizes its one buffer as integer-1 areas of 4,096 bytes (HostFile.InputOutputAreaBuffer); without the clause the implementor's count is one (DOC-A.1-164). Counts above 524,287 are refused (COBOL2897) and were not probed at run time under the host-safety rule.
